hypotheses.falsification: Replicate or closely match settings across draw rates; consistently equal or greater peak area at 0.5–0.9 mL/min than at moderately faster rates would challenge the claim in the tested setting.

hypotheses.claim: If waiting allows the sample and fluid path to settle before transfer, waiting 7–10 s may improve peak area relative to shorter waits at otherwise comparable injection settings; the observed contrast is confounded and does not establish this effect.
hypotheses.falsification: Compare repeated or closely matched conditions differing principally in wait time, including waits below 7 s and in 7–10 s; consistently equal or lower peak area for the longer waits would challenge the proposed advantage in the tested range.

hypotheses.claim: If a larger additional draw volume improves loop filling, additional volumes of 0.045–0.060 mL may produce larger peak areas than lower volumes at otherwise comparable injection settings; the available high-area observations are confounded by the other settings.
hypotheses.falsification: Compare replicated or closely matched injections inside and below the specified additional-volume range; consistently equal or lower peak areas inside the range would challenge the proposed filling advantage in those tested conditions.

hypotheses.claim: If higher pump frequency impairs transfer under these injection conditions, push speeds of 120–150 Hz may produce lower peak area than speeds below 120 Hz under otherwise comparable conditions. The observed contrast is confounded and does not identify a causal speed effect.
hypotheses.falsification: In replicated or closely matched injections varying primarily push speed, consistently equal or higher peak areas at 120–150 Hz than below 120 Hz would challenge this proposed transfer disadvantage in the tested range.

hypotheses.claim: At sample-pump draw rates of 0.5–1.0 mL/min, incomplete or dispersed filling and transfer may produce lower peak area than at moderately higher draw rates when other settings are comparable; the existing observations are confounded and do not establish causality.
hypotheses.falsification: Compare several closely matched conditions with draw rates inside and above this range; repeated comparable or higher peak areas at low flow would challenge the proposed disadvantage over those tested conditions.

hypotheses.claim: For otherwise comparable injection settings, tubing volumes of 0.65–0.9 mL may reduce peak area relative to approximately 0.3–0.4 mL if longer transfer promotes sample dispersion or incomplete delivery. The existing comparisons change other settings and cannot establish the mechanism.
hypotheses.falsification: Compare several closely matched settings across the two tubing-volume ranges, preferably with replicates; consistently comparable or larger peak areas with 0.65–0.9 mL would challenge the proposed disadvantage in the tested settings.

hypotheses.claim: At 105–120 °C with either specified bulky phosphine, pivalate may give higher yields than acetate with the same counterion and otherwise matched conditions, potentially through carboxylate-assisted C–H activation.
hypotheses.falsification: Across three matched pivalate-versus-acetate comparisons with the same counterion and other inputs, revise the claim if the mean pivalate-minus-acetate yield is at most −5 percentage points and at least two comparisons favor acetate.

hypotheses.claim: With the specified bulky dicyclohexyl biaryl phosphine and potassium or cesium pivalate, butyl acetate may give higher yield than p-xylene under otherwise matched conditions. The single matched comparison supports this possibility for potassium pivalate at 105 °C and 0.1 mol/L; extension to other settings is untested.
hypotheses.falsification: Revise the solvent claim if, across three matched butyl acetate versus p-xylene comparisons with this ligand and either pivalate salt, at least two favor p-xylene and the mean butyl acetate-minus-p-xylene yield is at most −5 percentage points.

hypotheses.claim: With the specified bulky dicyclohexyl biaryl phosphine and potassium or cesium pivalate, 120 °C may give higher yield than 105 °C under otherwise matched conditions. The temperature effect is unmeasured; the 105 °C observations establish only a starting point.
hypotheses.falsification: Revise the temperature claim if, across three matched 120 versus 105 °C comparisons within these base and ligand choices, at least two favor 105 °C and the mean 120-minus-105 °C yield is at most −5 percentage points.

hypotheses.claim: At 120 °C, N,N-dimethylacetamide may give yields below 40% with either specified bulky phosphine and potassium or cesium pivalate. This is an uncertain solvent-dependent association, not an established general inhibition mechanism; concentrations other than 0.057 mol/L are untested.
hypotheses.falsification: Revise the low-yield claim if two additional in-scope experiments each report at least 40% yield.

hypotheses.claim: For these fixed, unspecified coupling partners, the selected bulky dicyclohexyl biaryl phosphines may give higher yields than triphenylphosphine under otherwise matched conditions.
hypotheses.falsification: Test at least four matched pairs spanning more than one base or solvent, each comparing a scoped ligand with triphenylphosphine at the same concentration and temperature. A nonpositive median scoped-ligand minus triphenylphosphine yield difference would falsify the proposed advantage over those tested conditions.

hypotheses.claim: With potassium acetate in butyl acetate at 105–120 °C, the specified tris(furyl) phosphine may give lower yields than the specified bulky dicyclohexyl biaryl phosphine at matched concentrations. This is a local extrapolation from one matched pair.
hypotheses.falsification: Compare the two ligands in at least three matched concentration–temperature pairs within the stated base and solvent. A median tris(furyl) minus biaryl yield difference of zero or greater would falsify the proposed advantage over those tested pairs.

hypotheses.claim: With cesium pivalate, the specified caged phosphine and N,N-dimethylacetamide, raising concentration from 0.1 to 0.153 mol/L may increase yield at matched temperatures between 90 and 120 °C. The concentration trend observed with a different ligand and base may not transfer.
hypotheses.falsification: Measure both concentrations at each of the three temperatures. A median yield difference, 0.153 minus 0.1 mol/L, of zero or less falsifies the proposed increase over these tested pairs.

hypotheses.claim: For these fixed but unspecified substrates, pivalate may support higher yields than acetate through carboxylate-assisted C–H activation, when counterion and other conditions are matched.
hypotheses.falsification: Reject this working preference if, in three distinct matched condition pairs, pivalate yields are each at least 10 percentage points below the corresponding acetate yields.

hypotheses.claim: With cesium pivalate, p-xylene, and the specified dicyclohexylphosphine-substituted biaryl ligand, concentrations of 0.1–0.153 mol/L may outperform 0.057 mol/L across the tested temperatures. At 105 °C, the observed yields were 39.81% at 0.057 mol/L and 73.93% at 0.153 mol/L; extension to other temperatures and 0.1 mol/L is untested.
hypotheses.falsification: Withdraw the proposed temperature-general concentration preference if matched measurements at both 90 and 120 °C show that 0.153 mol/L yields no more than 5 percentage points above 0.057 mol/L.

hypotheses.claim: At 0.153 mol/L in p-xylene with the specified dicyclohexylphosphine-substituted biaryl ligand, cesium acetate, cesium pivalate and potassium acetate may often give yields above 60% across 90–120 °C. At 105 °C the two cesium salts gave 76.63% and 73.93%; cesium pivalate gave 68.31% at 120 °C. Potassium acetate and the remaining temperatures are untested.
hypotheses.falsification: Withdraw the proposed robustness if at least two of the next three distinct, previously unmeasured conditions in this scope yield below 60%.

hypotheses.claim: With potassium pivalate at 90 °C, the two specified bulky phosphines may tend to give yields below 50% in N,N-dimethylacetamide or p-xylene across the available concentrations. Both observed combinations gave 0%, but solvent, ligand and concentration effects are not separately established.
hypotheses.falsification: Withdraw the low-yield tendency if at least two of the next three distinct previously unmeasured conditions in this scope yield 50% or more.

hypotheses.claim: Potassium pivalate may provide an effective carboxylate-assisted pathway for this fixed coupling. As an operational forecast, four diverse potassium-pivalate conditions will average at least 25% reported yield.
hypotheses.falsification: Test four preselected potassium-pivalate conditions spanning at least two ligands and two solvents. An average reported yield below 25% falsifies the operational forecast for that set, not the proposed mechanism universally.

hypotheses.claim: For this fixed coupling, triphenylphosphine may outperform methyldiphenylphosphine under otherwise matched conditions. At potassium pivalate, butanenitrile, 0.153 mol/L and 120 °C, the respective reported yields were 15.64% and 0%; generalization beyond that single comparison is uncertain.
hypotheses.falsification: Preselect four previously unmeasured matched settings spanning at least two solvents and two temperatures, and measure both ligands at each. A nonpositive mean triphenylphosphine-minus-methyldiphenylphosphine yield difference falsifies the operational claim for that set.

hypotheses.claim: In butanenitrile, cesium acetate may give higher yield than potassium pivalate at otherwise matched conditions. At 0.153 mol/L and 120 °C with triphenylphosphine, the observed yields were 19.64% and 15.64%, respectively. Salt-dependent solubility or carboxylate chemistry could contribute, but the two salt components are confounded.
hypotheses.falsification: Preselect four previously unmeasured matched salt comparisons in butanenitrile at 120 °C, spanning two ligands and two concentrations. A nonpositive mean cesium-acetate-minus-potassium-pivalate yield difference falsifies the claim for that test set.

hypotheses.claim: With triphenylphosphine in butanenitrile at 120 °C, at least three of four preselected unmeasured base–concentration combinations will give less than 40% yield. Solvent-dependent salt availability or catalyst behaviour may contribute, but the mechanism is unproven.
hypotheses.falsification: Preselect four unmeasured in-scope combinations spanning at least two bases. Two or more yields of 40% or higher falsify the stated four-test claim.

hypotheses.claim: With a bulky dicyclohexyl biaryl phosphine, pivalate may give higher yield than the corresponding acetate under otherwise matched conditions, through carboxylate-assisted C–H activation.
hypotheses.falsification: Revise the preference if three matched pivalate-versus-acetate comparisons, holding counterion, ligand, solvent, concentration and temperature fixed within each pair, each give pivalate yields at least 5 percentage points lower.

hypotheses.claim: In p-xylene, a bulky dicyclohexyl biaryl phosphine may give a higher yield than triphenylphosphine under otherwise matched conditions. One matched comparison supports this possibility, but it does not establish an advantage for both biaryl ligands or across all other settings.
hypotheses.falsification: Revise the preference if two further matched comparisons in p-xylene, each holding base, concentration and temperature fixed, give the biaryl phosphine at least 5 percentage points lower yield than triphenylphosphine.

hypotheses.claim: With acetate, the specified dicyclohexyl biaryl phosphine and p-xylene, 0.153 mol/L may yield more than 0.057 mol/L under otherwise matched conditions. The two observed high-concentration acetate yields are encouraging, but comparisons with low-concentration pivalate also change the base and therefore do not establish a concentration effect.
hypotheses.falsification: Revise the concentration preference if two matched acetate comparisons, each holding counterion, ligand, solvent and temperature fixed, show that 0.153 mol/L yields at least 5 percentage points less than 0.057 mol/L.

hypotheses.claim: At 105 °C, the specified fluorinated biaryl phosphine with acetate in N,N-dimethylacetamide may retain high yield across the available concentrations and either acetate counterion. The cesium and concentration extrapolations are unmeasured.
hypotheses.falsification: Revise the high-yield claim if two of the next three unmeasured in-scope conditions yield below 80%.

hypotheses.claim: At 105–120 °C, the selected bulky phosphines may support higher palladium-catalysed arylation yields than triphenylphosphine under otherwise matched conditions.
hypotheses.falsification: Test at least four matched pairs against triphenylphosphine, covering at least two selected ligands. The proposed advantage is contradicted if the mean paired yield difference is zero or negative.

hypotheses.claim: With cesium pivalate and butyl acetate, the non-methoxylated dicyclohexylphosphino triisopropylbiphenyl ligand gives higher yield on average than its dimethoxy analogue at matched concentrations and temperatures. The single observed matched pair supports this local association, not a general mechanistic conclusion.
hypotheses.falsification: Compare at least three matched ligand pairs in this base and solvent across different concentration or temperature settings, including the existing pair. The claim is contradicted if the mean yield difference, non-methoxylated minus dimethoxy, is zero or negative.

hypotheses.claim: For the specified dicyclohexylphosphino triisopropylbiphenyl ligand with cesium or potassium pivalate, yields at 90 °C will average lower than at 105 °C under matched solvent and concentration conditions. The single matched cesium pivalate/butyl acetate pair gave 3.00% at 90 °C versus 59.92% at 105 °C; extension to the other settings is provisional.
hypotheses.falsification: Test at least four matched 90 °C versus 105 °C pairs, including the existing pair and covering both bases and both solvents. The claim is contradicted if the mean paired yield difference, 90 °C minus 105 °C, is zero or positive.

hypotheses.claim: Under the fixed protocol, pivalate bases may give higher mean yields than acetate bases at matched cation, ligand, solvent, concentration and temperature, potentially through carboxylate-assisted C–H activation.
hypotheses.falsification: Test at least four preselected matched pivalate–acetate pairs spanning different ligands or solvents. The proposed average advantage is contradicted if the mean pivalate-minus-acetate yield difference is zero or negative.

hypotheses.claim: With cesium acetate in butyl acetate, raising temperature from 90 to 105 or 120 °C may increase yield at matched ligand and concentration by accelerating reaction steps, although catalyst deactivation could offset this benefit.
hypotheses.falsification: Test at least four preselected matched pairs at 90 °C versus either 105 or 120 °C, spanning different ligands or concentrations. The proposed average benefit is contradicted if the mean higher-temperature-minus-90 °C yield difference is zero or negative.

hypotheses.claim: In butyl acetate at 105–120 °C, triphenylphosphine may give a higher average yield than methyldiphenylphosphine at matched base and concentration, potentially because the ligand substitution changes palladium coordination. The observed advantage at one cesium acetate condition may not generalize.
hypotheses.falsification: Measure at least four additional preselected matched ligand pairs spanning bases or concentrations within 105–120 °C. A mean triphenylphosphine-minus-methyldiphenylphosphine yield difference of zero or less contradicts the proposed average advantage in those pairs.

hypotheses.claim: With triphenylphosphine in N,N-dimethylacetamide at 120 °C and 0.1 or 0.153 mol/L, the remaining carboxylate-base conditions may average at least 75% yield. Solvent effects on the reaction environment are a possible explanation, not an established mechanism.
hypotheses.falsification: Preselect and measure four previously unmeasured conditions in the scope. An average yield below 75% contradicts the proposed high-yield expectation for that set.

hypotheses.claim: For these fixed, unspecified substrates, pivalate may give higher yields than acetate with the same counterion and otherwise matched conditions, if carboxylate-assisted C–H cleavage is important.
hypotheses.falsification: Test at least three pivalate–acetate pairs matched on counterion and all other inputs; an average pivalate-minus-acetate yield difference of zero or less would contradict the proposed advantage in those tested conditions.

hypotheses.claim: With cesium pivalate and the specified cyclic phosphine, butanenitrile may give higher yields than butyl acetate at 105–120 °C across the available concentrations. Solvent effects on catalyst speciation or base availability are possible explanations, not established mechanisms.
hypotheses.falsification: Across at least three matched nitrile–butyl acetate pairs within these temperatures and concentrations, an average nitrile-minus-ester yield difference of zero or less would contradict the proposed advantage. Ester comparisons require tests outside the favour scope.

hypotheses.claim: At 120 °C in butanenitrile and 0.057–0.1 mol/L, the specified cyclic phosphine may typically give at least 70% yield across the available carboxylate bases and outperform triphenylphosphine in matched conditions. Ligand-dependent catalyst speciation is a possible, unestablished explanation.
hypotheses.falsification: An average yield below 70% across at least three distinct in-scope conditions would contradict the yield claim. An average cyclic-phosphine-minus-triphenylphosphine difference of zero or less across at least three matched pairs would contradict the ligand advantage; those controls require tests outside the favour scope.

hypotheses.claim: At 120 °C in butanenitrile, the specified fluorinated phosphine may typically yield below 60% across carboxylate bases and concentrations, and may underperform the specified cyclic phosphine. Ligand-dependent catalyst speciation is a possible but unestablished explanation.
hypotheses.falsification: A mean yield of at least 60% across three distinct in-scope base–concentration conditions would contradict the yield claim. A cyclic-phosphine-minus-fluorinated-phosphine mean difference of zero or less across three matched pairs would contradict the comparative claim; those controls are outside the avoid scope.
